CrossChunkHistoryPressure.Finding: Hot mutations in another chunk evicted the cold chunk's needed delta from the single global pool.

ArchitectureDisposition.Outcome: Outcome B — reject history-derived latest-state as the fundamental steady-state model.
ArchitectureDisposition.BaselineAndRebaseInterpretation: A complete current-state introduction is expected for first knowledge of an AOI scope; a current-state rebase is expected when retained history can no longer bridge a gap. The audit targets recipient-specific history reconstruction after a proven baseline.
ArchitectureDisposition.CurrentModel: ChunkPublicationStore owns packed current rows plus one globally bounded, per-mutation history pool. A recipient owns per-chunk applied revision. Every ordinary delta request walks that chunk's retained list from its head, skips entries at/before the cursor, collapses later mutations by public slot, rereads current positive rows, and sorts output.
ArchitectureDisposition.CurrentIntroductionPath: A new subscription has TrackingOrigin/current interest but HasKnowledge=false and no applied cursor. It copies current relevant chunk truth at revision R0; only local commit or a matching authenticated remote proof advances applied knowledge to R0. Mutations after R0 remain delta debt. History-floor loss performs the same current-state operation as an explicit rebase but is diagnosed separately.
SourceTruthVersusRecipientObligation: source truth: source epoch, chunk key, from/to revisions, immutable current records, content hash
recipient obligation: session/generation, delivery ID, queue admission, proof ticket, applied revision, absence debt, retry/recovery state
ArchitectureDisposition.V2Comparison: V2 encoded an authoritative entity payload once, retained/coalesced latest state by (item, scope), and reused immutable payloads across scope subscribers. Per connection it still filtered relevant latest snapshots and tracked last-sent—not applied—sequences. Its source preparation is useful precedent; its sent-based knowledge and different transport/scheduler semantics are not acceptable V3 semantics.
LatestStateVersusEventHistory: latest/current state: public transform, prefab/body identity, orientation, visibility/ground-item flags, public presentation/equipment metadata, owner-private current state
event/occurrence history: Chat occurrences, Game application events, transactional results, and any future fact whose intermediate occurrence must be observed
ArchitectureDisposition.RemovalAndAbsenceRequirement: Positive current truth may be superseded by a later proven current version. Removal is not discoverable by scanning only present rows, so an alternative requires explicit recipient-local absence debt or immutable source tombstone/removal publication with independent exact proof. PF4B positive supersession cannot erase negative obligations.
ArchitectureDisposition.IntroductionRaceInvariant: Capture Introduction(C,R0) while proven knowledge is none; retain every semantically required mutation/removal newer than R0; proving R0 may establish only R0; AOI leave, epoch reset, or reconnect must fence the old offer and must never inherit its proof.

RecipientKnowledgeMemoryEstimate.Qualification: Design estimates only; array/object headers, indexes, alignment, proof debt, and capacity slack are excluded.

ArchitectureDisposition.RecommendedNextCheckpoint: Design the explicit Introduction/Rebase + shared immutable current/latest source publication model. Retain bounded history only as an ordinary lag bridge and retain independent recipient queue/delivery/proof/absence state. Do not add a range cache first.
ArchitectureDisposition.Pf6Disposition: PAUSED — PF6 should resume after the replication-model design/implementation checkpoint re-establishes the accepted correctness and product gates.
